static_traits.name: Li Jing
static_traits.family_status: Father works at Stifle, without siblings
static_traits.social_status: Has several close friends but has not yet shared feelings, recently distant from friends and family
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; without previous psychotherapy experience; similar problems had not appeared in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good cooperation, able to describe feelings and events specifically, neutral attitude

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling overwhelmed and frustrated because the last of four crime puzzles cannot yet be solved, which has led to a sense of failure and depression.
basic_info.core_demands: I want to stop seeing myself as a failure and return to a normal state; these feelings have significantly affected my daily life and work performance, and I hope to get relief.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough / have no ability

special_situations.event: While trying to solve four crime puzzles, the last one cannot yet be solved (the first three already succeeded)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot solve all the puzzles, the previous successes do not count, I am just a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Distracting attention by listening to music and smoking marijuana to escape the sense of failure, temporarily no longer trying that puzzle
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not smart enough, I am a failure, all efforts were in vain

special_situations.event: When repeatedly thinking about that unsolved puzzle or participating in similar puzzle activities
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I encounter a similar difficult problem again, I will definitely fail; failure means I am not capable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids or delays participating in similar challenges to reduce the possibility of failing again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will definitely fail again, I am not capable

special_situations.event: Difficulty concentrating at work; performance declines
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If work performance is not good, it proves my overall ability is insufficient, I am worthless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Distances himself from friends and family; reduces others' evaluations and contact
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My work is also not done well, I am worthless

special_situations.event: Facing opportunities to communicate with friends or family and share troubles
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I express distress to friends, I will burden them and they may look down on me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Choosing not to share, keeping isolated to avoid 'troubling' others
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should not trouble others, they will be dragged down by me

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized as capable and worthy of respect; hopes to maintain self-worth and confidence
core_conflict.fear: Afraid of being looked down on after failure, being judged as incompetent, becoming a burden to others
defense_goal: Reduces the risk of being evaluated through distance and avoidance
Controlling anxiety and shame with distraction and self-denial
Not seeking help from others to maintain surface-level safety

object_relations.self_representation: Seeing oneself as a failure / burden
object_relations.object_representation: Regarding others as people who may look down on oneself and be dragged down by oneself

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When advised to share troubles with family and friends or seek support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Subconsciously believing that family and friends will be dragged down by oneself and will look down on oneself (projective interpretation)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Politely declining to share, emphasizing 'I should not trouble others', calm tone but avoiding talking deeply about others' support

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about failure experiences or being asked to try a challenge again
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing one failure equals overall incompetence, must stay away to avoid being frustrated again
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using self-deprecating wording (such as 'I am not smart enough'), low tone, reducing communication and participation

manifestations: Treating one unsolved puzzle as negating the previous three successes, feeling 'all efforts were in vain'
Hard to gain meaning and value from achievements
outcomes: Worsening feelings of failure and frustration
Reduced motivation and declining work performance

manifestations: Actively distancing from friends and family, not sharing feelings
Not seeking help for fear of 'troubling' others

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains impulses originally wanting to express or act toward others or the environment, and does it to themselves instead, drawing the energy inward
manifestations: Having close friends but choosing not to share failure and depression
Pressing the need that could have been directed outward for support back onto myself, bearing it alone

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'
manifestations: Self-demanding 'I should not trouble others', treating not disturbing others as a hard rule
Evaluating oneself by the standard of 'only completing everything counts as success'

exception_events.target_problem: When facing difficult puzzles, the client usually catastrophizes a single failure, negates past successes, and develops self-denial and avoidance
exception_events.unique_outcome: In the first three puzzles of the same series, the client solved them successfully and felt proud and capable, without self-denial appearing
exception_events.reason: Different understanding: the self-talk at the time was 'I am capable, I am good at this'; different situation: the puzzles matched their ability, engagement was high

positive_force: Multiple successful experiences on similar tasks (the first three puzzles)
Willing to try different cognitive and behavioral methods (willing to do behavioral experiments)
Has a few close friends as potential support resources
Can clearly express inner experiences and is willing to seek counseling
negative_force: Thinking patterns of catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, and overgeneralization
Mental filtering: focuses only on one failure and ignores successes
Overly binding self-worth to a single outcome, seeking external validation
Using ineffective coping strategies (music, smoking marijuana) keeps the problem going

target_behavior.behavior: Self-labeling and self-denial (such as 'I am a failure''I am not smart enough')
antecedent: Participating in similar puzzle or challenge activities
target_behavior.core_reason: Equating one failure with insufficient overall ability, with black-and-white, overgeneralizing, and mental-filtering cognition
target_behavior.function: In the short term maintains his self-explanatory framework and avoids trying again to escape the sense of failure
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood, decreased drive, work performance impaired

target_behavior.behavior: Social avoidance and isolation (not sharing distress with friends and family)
antecedent: When thinking of confiding in friends or entering social settings
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying about being looked down on or troubling others; fear of evaluation and shame
target_behavior.function: Escaping others' evaluations and potential negative feedback, maintaining a surface sense of security
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased support, loneliness worsened, emotional problems maintained

target_behavior.behavior: Distracting attention with substances and music (smoking marijuana, listening to music)
antecedent: When feeling failure, depression, and helplessness
target_behavior.core_reason: Seeks ways to quickly relieve negative emotions and feelings of failure
target_behavior.consequence: The problem has not yet been solved, possibly further affecting sleep, focus, and work performance

antecedent: Persistently ruminating on failure and frustration
target_behavior.core_reason: Physiological and routine dysregulation driven by frustration and anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Physical condition declined, attention and work performance further impaired
